title: Best Online Healthcare Directive Services Compared (2026)
metaDescription: Six ways to make a living will or healthcare power of attorney online, compared on price, documents and attorney access, from free to a $499 trust plan.
h1: Best Online Healthcare Directive Services Compared
introText:
The best online healthcare directive services are [FreeWill](https://www.freewill.com/) (free), [Five Wishes](https://www.fivewishes.org/products/five-wishes-paper) ($5 per paper copy), [LegalZoom](https://www.legalzoom.com/personal/estate-planning/living-will-overview.html) ($39 or $49), [Mama Bear Legal Forms](https://www.mamabearlegalforms.com/) ($159 will package), [Trust & Will](https://www.trustandwill.com/pricing) (will package from $199) and [Rocket Lawyer](https://www.rocketlawyer.com/family-and-personal/health-and-medical/healthcare-decisions/document/living-will/co) (free template on a 7-day trial, then membership). A living will states your wishes about medical treatment. A healthcare power of attorney names a person to make decisions for you.

At ModernWallet, we compared these six services using only what each one publishes on its own page: the price, the documents included and any attorney access. Trust & Will sells its living will only inside a will or trust package. Mama Bear Legal Forms puts its health care power of attorney inside a will package.

If you also want a will, our [online will maker roundup](/roundup/best-online-will-makers/) compares those packages. The [will cost calculator](/estate-planning/will-cost-calculator/) lets you add up the total before you buy.
rankingCriteria: Each service is compared on four factors: price, the documents included, attorney access, and what its page says about state rules. Price covers the full shape of the cost, including trials that renew, add-ons and bulk rates. The six services are listed in a fixed order that is not a quality ranking, and each gets a "best for" label drawn from what its own page publishes.

options.name: FreeWill
options.bestFor: People who want a free healthcare directive with no credit card
options.description: FreeWill offers an advance healthcare directive, which FreeWill also calls a living will. The document lets you state your healthcare wishes and appoint someone to make decisions for you if you are unable to. FreeWill's page says its estate planning tools are "100% free" with no credit card required, at "absolutely no cost to you." A Durable Financial Power of Attorney is a separate FreeWill product for naming someone to make financial decisions if you can't. Only FreeWill's Revocable Living Trust carries a "California only" label, and the page lists no state restriction for the healthcare directive.

One directive covers both your healthcare wishes and the person you appoint to decide
Offers a separate Durable Financial Power of Attorney for money decisions
Lists no state restriction for the healthcare directive

FreeWill's page lists no attorney consultation for the healthcare directive
The Revocable Living Trust is labelled California only

options.name: LegalZoom
options.bestFor: People who want a standalone living will and healthcare power of attorney with optional attorney calls
options.description: LegalZoom sells two healthcare directive tiers. The $39 Basic Healthcare Directive includes a living will, a healthcare power of attorney, online questions to guide you, unlimited revisions for 30 days and secure online document storage. The $49 Premium Healthcare Directive adds unlimited 30-minute attorney consultations for 14 days. After that trial, the attorney subscription renews at $25 per month unless you cancel online or by phone. Documents are typically ready to download in 2 to 3 business days, and LegalZoom says they were created by attorneys and "have been accepted in all 50 states."

options.name: Trust & Will
options.bestFor: People who want a living will inside a will or trust package
options.description: Trust & Will does not list a standalone price for a living will, healthcare directive or power of attorney, because those documents come only in packages. The Will Plan, starting at $199, includes a HIPAA Authorization, a Living Will and a Power of Attorney alongside a Last Will & Testament. The Trust Plan, starting at $499, adds a Revocable Living Trust, Pour Over Will, Schedule of Assets, Certification of Trust and Trust Funding Guide. Both plans come in Individual or Couple versions and offer payment plans. Two add-ons are optional: a Membership at $49 per year and Attorney Support at +$299.

options.name: Mama Bear Legal Forms

options.description: Mama Bear Legal Forms bundles healthcare documents with its Last Will & Testament package. The package costs $159 for an individual or $249 for a married couple, and adding a spouse's will costs $90. It includes a last will and testament, a health care power of attorney, a finance power of attorney and a HIPAA release, though the page does not list a living will by name. A separate $89 College Power of Attorney includes health and finance power of attorney documents, a HIPAA release and a FERPA waiver, to help a college-age student in an emergency. A Senior Adult Power of Attorney also costs $89, and the page gives only its title and price.

verdict:
Pick FreeWill if you want a healthcare directive that costs nothing and needs no credit card. Pick LegalZoom if you want a living will and healthcare power of attorney as a standalone $39 purchase, or $49 with 14 days of attorney consultations. Pick Trust & Will if you want a living will, power of attorney and HIPAA authorization inside a will package starting at $199.

Pick Mama Bear Legal Forms if you want health care and finance powers of attorney with a $159 will, or the $89 College Power of Attorney for a college-age student. Pick Rocket Lawyer if you want a state living will template and an attorney reply within one business day, and you can accept a membership price the page does not publish. Pick Five Wishes if you want a plain-language paper form at $5 a copy.

FreeWill, Mama Bear Legal Forms and Five Wishes list no attorney consultation, so skip them if you want a lawyer to answer questions before you sign. LegalZoom Premium, Trust & Will's +$299 Attorney Support and Rocket Lawyer's attorney questions cover that need.

sections.heading: Living Will vs. Healthcare Power of Attorney
sections.content:
A living will states your wishes about medical treatment, while a healthcare power of attorney names a person to make decisions for you. Several of these services sell the two together under the name healthcare directive or advance directive.

LegalZoom's $39 Basic Healthcare Directive includes both a living will and a healthcare power of attorney. FreeWill's advance healthcare directive, which FreeWill also calls a living will, lets you state your wishes and appoint someone to decide for you. Trust & Will's Will Plan lists a Living Will and a Power of Attorney as separate documents in the same package.

Mama Bear Legal Forms works differently. Its $159 will package includes a health care power of attorney and a HIPAA release, but the page does not list a living will by name. Rocket Lawyer's page describes a living will template, and Five Wishes calls its paper form both an advance directive and a living will.

A financial power of attorney names someone to make money decisions and is a separate document from the healthcare one. FreeWill offers its Durable Financial Power of Attorney as its own product, and Mama Bear Legal Forms puts a finance power of attorney in its will package. For how these documents differ from a will, see our [power of attorney vs. will comparison](/compare/power-of-attorney-vs-will/), and for the court-appointed route, see [power of attorney vs. guardianship](/compare/power-of-attorney-vs-guardianship/).

sections.heading: Signing and Witness Rules
sections.content:
Signing rules for healthcare directives, including witnesses and notarization, vary by state. LegalZoom's page says its documents were created by attorneys and "have been accepted in all 50 states." LegalZoom also says many states require notarization and tells you to look up your own state's signing rules, but its page does not list them state by state.

Five Wishes' page gives no list of states where its paper form is valid. Rocket Lawyer uses a state selector that includes the District of Columbia, and its Colorado page says the Colorado form can be used throughout Colorado. FreeWill lists no state restriction for its healthcare directive, and only its Revocable Living Trust is marked California only.

Before you sign any of these documents, find out whether your state asks for witnesses, a notary, or both. If you can't tell which rules apply, a lawyer in your state can answer that question. The next section lists the attorney options these six services sell.

sections.heading: When a Lawyer Is the Better Route
sections.content:
A lawyer is the better route when you cannot tell which signing rules your state applies to a healthcare directive. Three of these services offer attorney access alongside the documents.

- LegalZoom Premium costs $49 for unlimited 30-minute attorney consultations over 14 days. After the trial, the subscription renews at $25 per month unless you cancel online or by phone. Consultations are limited to one per new legal matter and exclude business matters.
- Trust & Will sells Attorney Support as a +$299 add-on.
- Rocket Lawyer lets you ask an attorney a question and get a response within one business day, or request a more in-depth document review. The page gives no price for either, and it does not say whether "Consult an Attorney Live" is part of the 7-day trial.

FreeWill, Mama Bear Legal Forms and Five Wishes list no attorney consultation on their pages. To weigh hiring a lawyer directly against an online service, read our [online will vs. lawyer comparison](/compare/online-will-vs-lawyer/), and for a full planning checklist, start with our [first-time estate planning guide](/guides/first-time-estate-planning/).

faqs.question: What is the difference between a living will and a healthcare directive?
faqs.answer: On these service pages the two terms often overlap. A living will states your wishes about medical treatment. FreeWill calls its advance healthcare directive a living will, and Five Wishes calls its form both an advance directive and a living will. LegalZoom's Healthcare Directive pairs a living will with a healthcare power of attorney, which names a person to decide for you.

faqs.question: Can I make a healthcare directive online for free?
faqs.answer: Yes. FreeWill's page says its estate planning tools, including its advance healthcare directive, are 100% free with no credit card required. Rocket Lawyer describes a free living will template that comes with a 7-day free trial, but its page does not state the membership price after the trial. Five Wishes costs $5 per paper copy.

faqs.question: Do I need a lawyer or notary to sign a healthcare directive?
faqs.answer: Notary and witness rules vary by state, and LegalZoom's page says many states require notarization. You can make a directive without paying for attorney time on FreeWill, LegalZoom Basic or Five Wishes. If you want an attorney to answer questions, LegalZoom Premium adds 14 days of consultations for $49, and Trust & Will sells Attorney Support for +$299.

faqs.question: How much does an online healthcare directive cost?
faqs.answer: Online healthcare directives on this list range from free to packages starting at $199. FreeWill is free, Five Wishes is $5 per copy, and LegalZoom is $39 or $49. Mama Bear Legal Forms includes a health care power of attorney in a $159 will package or an $89 power of attorney set. Trust & Will's Will Plan starts at $199, and Rocket Lawyer's membership price after its 7-day trial is not published.

faqs.question: Is an online living will valid in every state?
faqs.answer: Signing rules vary by state, so a living will has to be signed the way your state requires. LegalZoom's page says its documents have been accepted in all 50 states and also says many states require notarization. Rocket Lawyer offers state living wills through a selector that includes the District of Columbia. FreeWill lists no state restriction for its healthcare directive, and Five Wishes' page gives no per-state validity list.
